scope: Deployment-context follow-up; reported conclusions are kept separate from the captured RPC evidence.

cases.name: QuickMiney A
cases.evidenceStatus: independently captured from two public RPC origins at BNB block 135300331; severity is an analyst assessment of this initializer path
cases.summary: The named proxy stores implementation A, has consumed initialization, has populated orcale authority, and rejects the tested initializer with the already-initialized error. Implementation A still accepts its own initializer simulation. This supports implementation hardening; no live-proxy takeover through this initializer was demonstrated.
cases.recommendation: For future implementation releases, add an initialization lock compatible with this custom Initializable base and verify proxy storage-layout compatibility and fresh-proxy initialization. The supplied source does not define _disableInitializers(), so the generic OpenZeppelin constructor snippet is not a drop-in fix.
limitations: This verifies one named proxy and the tested initializer path at the recorded block; it is not a full audit or an exhaustive proxy inventory.
The admin slot is a storage observation; actual upgrade semantics require version-specific runtime/source verification.
Native BNB and one named ERC-20 were measured. Other token/assets are not inventoried.
QuickMiney B has no linked proxy independently established in this record. The three Referral cases remain separately unclassified.
The Firelight comparison was supplied by the user and is not the basis of the independent captured evidence.
verifiedChecks: The named proxy implementation slot agrees on implementation A across both RPC origins.
The proxy's initialized field is one and its authority fields are populated.
The proxy's initializer simulation reverts with an already-initialized error.
cases.authority: The observed admin slot and effective orcale field point to the same code-empty address. This records concentrated authority, not a missing-authority vulnerability.
